title: Mitigate client-encoded-length vs tokenizer mismatch for emoji/wide-char inputs causing misbilling
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing a class of misbilling where client-side length heuristics (used for provisional rate limiting / precharging and UI quota feedback) are based on encoded byte/char counts (UTF-16/JavaScript string length or raw byte length after client compression) while server metering uses the canonical BPE tokenizer. This mismatch is most visible for emoji-heavy content, combined diacritics, and East Asian fullwidth characters. The result: customers see higher provisional debits, unexpected rate-limit rejections, and in some cases retroactive billing corrections which erode trust.

Why it matters: provisional client-side accounting drives UX (quota bars, early rate-limit decisions) and some gateways pre-allocate credits; disconnects create user-visible overcharges or surprising soft-fails during streaming. We need a robust solution that minimizes client changes, keeps server metering authoritative, and provides smooth migration for existing SDK consumers.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use JS SDK to send an emoji-heavy prompt (e.g., 40 emoji or sequences of combined emoji + skin tones).
2) Observe client-reported 'estimated tokens' in devtools (SDK pre-tokenizer uses code-point length heuristic).
3) Start a streaming request that hits provisional rate limit using the client estimate and is precharged.
4) On server-side finalization, canonical tokenizer reports a lower/higher token count; check billing ledger and client quota state for adjustments and any retroactive refunds or chargebacks.
5) Repeat with UTF-16 surrogate pairs, ZWJ sequences, and mixed languages to characterize variance.
observed_behavior: Client provisional estimates are often off by +5% to +120% for inputs with many emoji/ZWJ sequences. This causes provisional precharge that is later adjusted on the server, leading to customer disputes and quota UX inconsistencies.
expected_behavior: Provisional client estimates should be within a bounded delta of server tokenizer (prefer <=10% variance for 99th pct of inputs), and when variance exceeds threshold we should correct precharged credits without customer-visible surprise.
impact: Medium — affects a non-trivial subset of customers (messaging apps, social products, non-Latin locales). It causes UX confusion, increased support tickets, and occasional incorrect provisional rate-limits during streaming sessions.
proposed_solution: Short term: implement a server-side reconciliation hook that, on finalization, computes delta between provisional client estimate and canonical token count and issues a background adjustment (refund or charge). Surface an 'adjusted' event on the session channel so SDK can update quota UI without disrupting the stream.

Medium term: add an SDK pretokenizer that mirrors server canonicalizer semantics for common languages and encodings; ship as opt-in in next minor SDK. The SDK will send a checksum of the prompt pretokenization to allow lightweight server-side verification without re-tokenizing on hot paths.

Long term: publish a documented 'pretokenization contract' used by SDKs and third-party proxies. Provide a telemetry-derived mapping for problematic character classes (ZWJ/emoji sequences, combining marks, CJK ideographs) and expose a server-side fast-path to normalize client estimates for these classes when checksum missing.

Telemetry & detection: add an alert on the token-estimate-delta metric (server_tokens - client_estimate) and a dashboard segmented by input character class and region. Flag sessions where delta > 25% for >5 requests per account for manual review.

Migration: phased rollout where server reconciliation runs for all streams but SDK pretokenizer is optional for first 2 cycles. Provide automatic 'soft-correct' mode that only informs SDK, and 'hard-correct' that adjusts account ledgers after 2026-04-15 when we have one full cycle of telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server reconciliation implemented and running in canary region without causing increased tokenization latency on hot paths.
2) Dashboard showing token-estimate-delta with breakdown by unicode class is available to SRE/MPM team.
3) SDK pretokenizer prototype published (JS + Python) and passes interop tests against server canonicalizer for 95% of sampled inputs in internal corpus.
4) Customer-visible quota UI no longer shows provisional overcharge in >90% of detected emoji-heavy sessions after soft-correct rollout.
5) Documentation page describing pretokenization contract and migration plan published and linked from SDK changelog.
notes: We must avoid re-tokenizing on the hot path in the serving runtime to prevent added latency. The reconciliation process should be eventual and idempotent; design ledger adjustments as compensating entries rather than destructive edits to historical invoices.
